evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/account/listings/[id]/edit/page.tsx — the authenticated listing-edit page renders almost entirely hardcoded Slovak strings in a 4-locale portal (en/sk/cs/de, routed under [locale]). The file only resolves i18n 5 times yet the whole form is Slovak-literal: L166 load-error fallback 'Načítanie inzerátu zlyhalo.', L213 save-error fallback 'Uloženie zlyhalo, skúste znova.', L429 label 'Adresa' / placeholder 'Ulica a číslo', L432 'Mesto / Obec', L465 'Plocha (m²)', L466 'Počet izieb', L469 'Rok výstavby', L827 button 'Ukladám…' / 'Uložiť zmeny'.

Reachable in production: this is the owner's primary listing-edit screen (UC-51). An en/cs/de user who opens /en/account/listings/<id>/edit sees Slovak-only labels, placeholders and error copy — a real i18n regression against the portal's multi-language requirement. Net-new: 0 prior reality-web signal/backlog mentions of this file; it is not in any earlier Tier-1d signal set.

Fix (frontend-only, cloud-landable, no backend/DB): move the heading, field labels/placeholders, the two error fallbacks and the save-button copy into the reality-web messages namespace for en/sk/cs/de and resolve via next-intl useTranslations (already used elsewhere in this app). Severity low (i18n gap, +1).

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/import/CsvImport.tsx:58-64 — handleFileSelect (the <input type=file> onChange path) accepts ANY selected file and advances straight to the mapping step with no type check: `const selectedFile = e.target.files?.[0]; if (selectedFile) { setFile(selectedFile); setStep('mapping'); }`. The sibling drag-drop handler handleDrop (L47-56) DOES guard with `droppedFile?.type === 'text/csv' || droppedFile?.name.endsWith('.csv')`, so the two entry points are inconsistent.

The file input carries accept='.csv,text/csv' (L338) but `accept` is only a picker hint — a user can switch the dialog to All Files and pick a .xlsx/.png, which then flows into useCsvPreview/useCsvImport with an empty-id guard `agency?.id || ''`. Not a crash (server + preview surface a parse error downstream), but a validation gap and a drop-vs-select behavioral inconsistency.

Fix (frontend-only, cloud-landable): apply the same type/extension guard used in handleDrop inside handleFileSelect, and surface a non-CSV rejection message instead of silently advancing. Severity low (+1).
